tweets: Price oracle manipulation exploits vulnerabilities in price feeds to alter contract logic, potentially causing unauthorized actions or fund loss.
To mitigate this risk, leverage multiple decentralized oracles rather than relying on a single data source.
Implement input validation to ensure all oracle data is properly checked before being used by your contract logic.
Aggregate prices from several DEXs or oracles using median or mean calculations to smooth out anomalies.
Reject outlier prices and anomalous deviations to prevent a single bad feed from skewing your pricing mechanism.
Use Time-Weighted Average Prices (TWAP) over sufficient windows to resist short-lived price manipulations.
Avoid basing core prices on illiquid pools, as they are more susceptible to manipulation during low volume.
Design fail-safe behaviors that halt sensitive operations like borrowing or liquidations when data is suspicious or unavailable.
Deploy circuit breakers and rate limiting on parameter changes to restrict how quickly prices can be altered.
Monitor price deviations between your oracle and reference markets, setting alerts for out-of-band movements.
